title: Latch-Based Clock Gate (ICG)
constraints: `gclk` = `clk` gated by the enable, with no glitches and no truncated pulses.
The enable `en | test_en` is captured by a **latch that is transparent while `clk` is low**. `gclk = clk & latched_enable`.

So an enable change while `clk` is high takes effect at the **next** rising edge, and a change while `clk` is low takes effect at the coming rising edge. `test_en` forces the clock on (for scan testing).
Latches are allowed (and required) here. Must be synthesizable.
hints: The latch holds its value during the whole high phase of `clk`, so the AND gate's other input can't change while `clk` is high.
In Verilog: `always @(*) if (!clk) en_l = en | test_en;`. That is an intentional latch.
A negedge flip-flop is **not** equivalent. It samples only at the falling edge, so it misses enable changes made later in the low phase.

examples.check: enable changes while clk is high
examples.title: no glitch
